domain: adult social care regulation / 12-month register-exit (deregistration) prediction
prediction_question: For a care home location active on the CQC register at monthly vintage T (the 'HSCA Active Locations' file produced on that date), will the location's registration end within the following 12 months (Location Status Inactive-Dereg with a Location HSCA End Date inside (T, T+365d])?
prediction_time: The production instant of a monthly CQC 'HSCA Active Locations' vintage (Europe/London; the date in the file name, e.g. '05 January 2024 HSCA Active Locations'; the weekly sibling CSV states 'This data was produced on <date>' - the same stamping convention). Features are the vintage's own columns only: HSCA start date, care home beds, service types (with/without nursing), service user bands, latest overall rating + its publication date (measured as-of: 0/14,765 care-home rows at T=2024-01-05 carry a rating publication date after T), geography, provider attributes incl. Companies House number. Target = the register event dated after T, read from the cumulative Deactivated Locations product. Archive: monthly vintages 2011-2026 (Drive year folders, anonymous).
target_definition: Binary: Location HSCA End Date in (T, T+365d]. Label source: CQC Deactivated Locations file (cumulative; Location HSCA End Date + Location Status; among care homes all-time: 17,046 Inactive-Dereg vs 131 Removed). Label-source columns never ship as features. Censoring: instants whose 12-month window extends past the deactivated file's coverage (2026-11-02 edition) are excluded. FRAMING: the target is the register event (deregistration of the location), which CQC notes can include services continuing under a new registration; not necessarily service cessation - see verdict.uncertainty.

construction_script: candidates/cqc-care-home-deregistration/source/build.py (stdlib-only; harvests the CQC 'HSCA Active Locations' January vintages 2016-2022 + 2024 + 2025 from the publisher's Drive archive plus the pinned 2026-11-02 Deactivated Locations edition, sha256-pinned per file; walks workbook order to the Location ID header sheet and drops no-header vintages loudly; per-instant pseudonymised ids (missing-successor P0 design); train 2018-2022 / eval 2024-01 / holdout 2025-01 with the (T, T+365d] deregistration label and 757 eval positives asserted; quality.json timing kind=period_end; source/run.sh then qualifies the FULL artifact with gate 1.5.0, exact-byte --accept, and only after that scores the train-only rate-table references)
split_strategy: Annual January instants with non-overlapping 12-month target windows. Proposed: train instants Jan 2016-2019 (targets 2016-2020), eval Jan 2020-2021 (targets 2020-2022), holdout Jan 2022-2024 (holdout target windows end by 2025-01, fully observed by the 2026-11-02 deactivated file). Instants 2011-2015 are usable for train with the pre-Oct-2014 no-ratings caveat; instants 2025+ are excluded while either the deactivated file's coverage or the publisher's migration-related cancellation lag is unresolved. Exact per-instant positives are the first construction measurement; measured anchor: T=2024-01-05 carries 14,765 eligible care homes and 758 positives (5.13%).

contracts.redistribution: supported - OGL v3.0 from the publisher's own instruments (using-cqc-data page, in-sheet statement, T&C page; licence_class A); no dataset-specific restriction; attribution and the in-sheet analysis-disclaimer carry to any release
contracts.prediction_timing: supported - monthly vintages 2011-2026 with production-date stamps; features vintage-visible; as-of measured (0/14,765 rating publication dates after T); dated worked example with real named homes on both label sides in notes.md (T = 2024-01-05, Europe/London)
contracts.obtainable_target: supported - Location HSCA End Date + Location Status from the cumulative Deactivated Locations file (whole event history back to 2010 in one product); label-source columns excludable; censoring policy stated; 'Removed' separated from 'Inactive-Dereg' (17,046 vs 131)
contracts.split_capacity: supported - measured per-year care-home deregistrations 697-1,656 every year 2011-2026 with a 5.13% measured prevalence at T=2024-01-05; proposed train/eval/holdout instant windows each carry thousands of eligible homes and hundreds of positives; clustering mild (376-877 distinct providers/year, top-3 share <= 12.2%); exact per-instant counts are named as the first construction measurement
contracts.not_a_mirror: supported (differentiated) - no scored, temporally-split ML-ready benchmark on CQC bulk data exists in catalogue or literature searches; prior art is econometric (BMJ Public Health 2024 logistic regression; Lancet Healthy Longevity involuntary-closures Stata/R replication package for the 816 enforced-closure subset; NIHR multilevel logit) or a different country/regulator (npj Health Systems US nursing-home closures); ours = the vintage-anchored prediction-instant contract, temporal splits, reference triad and gate-qualified artifact; see novelty_check

verdict.uncertainty: 1) FRAMING: the register event conflates cessation with re-registration - CQC's own file note says some deactivations continue under a new registration (legal entity/address/provider change), and BMJ 2024 (8,346 complete closures vs 14,911 register events 2011-2023) implies roughly 40-55% of deregistrations are re-registrations/transfer; advancement must either ship the honest register-event target with this limitation stated or build successor linkage (address/UPRN/ODS-code/brand adjacency; the API's linked-organisation data needs developer-portal auth). 2) HEADROOM UNMEASURED: simple references (last-rating rate, bed-size, LA, provider-sector) are the plausible strong priors - the BMJ/npj evidence says ratings+ownership drive closures (US ML AUROC 0.79 out-of-sample, so learnable structure exists); the reference triad is the FIRST construction measurement and the task is droppable if a one-line prior saturates it. 3) The publisher's system migration is delaying reflection of registration cancellations in current files - recent-window lag check required. 4) Era breaks: single-assessment rating change (~2024, location-level overall ratings dropped for multi-service ASC locations) and the 1 April 2019 regulatory-history inheritance change. 5) Provider-group cross-row exposure if group-history features ship - strictly-prior events only + declared restricted protocol. 6) Dormant-but-registered locations may sit in the at-T population (no dormancy flag in the bulk files; not measured this session).

novelty_check.theirs: CQC publishes the raw register (monthly active/deactivated bulk files, OGL v3); health-services research built bespoke API-linked panels for explanatory regressions - BMJ Public Health 2024 (29,548 homes, logistic regression, closure determinants), Lancet Healthy Longevity 2024 (816 CQC-enforced involuntary closures, Stata/R replication package), NIHR multilevel logit - and npj Health Systems predicts US nursing-home closures from CMS data; none ships a scored, temporally-split prediction benchmark
novelty_check.ours: vintage-anchored 12-month CQC care-home deregistration benchmark: monthly 2011-2026 register vintages with production-date prediction instants, strictly at-T features (beds, service types, service user bands, latest rating + publication date, provider attributes incl. Companies House number), temporal splits by instant year, reference triad, gate-qualified artifact; no prior ML-ready scored benchmark on UK CQC bulk data
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

framing_decision.target: 12-month deregistration of the CQC location: Location Status Inactive-Dereg or Removed with a Location HSCA End Date in (T, T+365d], joined from the Deactivated Locations file by Location ID
framing_decision.why: the register event is the publisher's own well-defined, predictable monthly-product event; successor-linked 'complete closure' targets need API auth or speculative address/brand adjacency that cannot be verified from the bulk files
framing_decision.limitation_stated: the register event conflates cessation with re-registration (CQC in-file note; BMJ 2024: 8,346 complete closures vs 14,911 register events 2011-2023 implies ~40-55% re-registrations) - carried in quality.json limitations and every package document

preflight_cqc_chd_001.row_selection: build_panel(): rows = 'Care home?' = Y rows of the T vintage (the vintage's own column, read at T); the label is looked up afterwards solely to compute the label; the 2023 January vintage is excluded by design so every train window closes >= 12 months before the eval instant; dropped-instant rule: a vintage whose required columns do not resolve is DROPPED with a loud diagnostic, train needs >= 5 resolved instants
preflight_cqc_chd_001.artifact_writer: write_artifact(): ONE column list (COLUMNS) in one place; location_key asserted unique across the panel; meta.json carries all 8 TASK_KEYS with per-split positive_rate
preflight_cqc_chd_001.qualification: run.sh stage 2: qualify_dataset.py (gate 1.5.0) on the FULL artifact on the worker; stage 3: --accept on the exact bytes; both before any reference is computed
preflight_cqc_chd_001.first_performance_metric: score.py (run.sh stage 4), post-acceptance, eval rows only, holdout never opened; build.py computes no AUC/accuracy/model (read line by line) - counts, fixture asserts and per-instant diagnostics only

p0_panel_design.successor_exposure: the missing-successor rule (the unhcr P0 class): killed STRUCTURALLY - every scored frame carries a SINGLE instant (train 2016-01..2022-01, eval 2024-01, holdout 2025-01, the last instant), so the successor rows of eval rows exist only in the sealed holdout and holdout rows have no successor instant in the artifact
p0_panel_design.identity: location identity ships as a per-instant pseudonym sha256(salt|instant|location_id)[:16]; no name, address, postcode, provider id, CH/charity number ships; real ids only in auxiliary/location_map.csv (staging-side, never solver-visible)
p0_panel_design.provider_features: no provider-group history feature ships; provider sector only
p0_panel_design.probes: gate probe 0: successor attack over the pseudonym id (expected coverage 0); probe 1: successor attack over the strongest instant-invariant quasi-key (LA x beds x start-year x rating x sector, +12-month offset) - coverage on eval/holdout is the measured bound over the frames a solver can see; in-train coverage measures the quasi-linkage rate where labels are public anyway
p0_panel_design.train_label_chronology: train instants stop at 2022: every train 12-month window closes by 2023-01-13, a year before the eval instant

preflight_cqc_chd_001.timing_block: kind=period_end, source_kind=administrative_record, lag 0 (the vintage IS the register state at its production instant); observations carry every vintage's production date; as-of asserted in-build (0/14,765 eval rows with rating Publication Date after T)
